items.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: I’m pleased to have drummer Vince Lateano with me today.

ctx.x: Drummer Vince Lateano was born in Sacramento, California. He was performing professionally while still in his teens and settled in San Francisco after military service. Vince has recorded and toured with a lengthy list of jazz luminaries including Vince Guaraldi, Woody Herman, Tania Maria and Cal Tjader. He has been a drum instructor for the Monterey Jazz Festival since Vince was interviewed in San Francisco, California on August 8, 2002 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in San Francisco. I’m pleased to have drummer Vince Lateano with me today. You know, when you come into town and you look at the local papers and stuff, it looks like there is a very active jazz scene here. But I wonder if it’s like that all the time.

Well people say that. They come in and just like what you’re saying, it can be deceiving. There is an active jazz scene. First I should say that. I mean there are a lot of people here that make their living playing jazz. But the listings sometimes, you have several listings and it might be music in a restaurant, which could be jazz but also could be wallpaper. And we’ve all been there, and there is a difference.
